parsed.explanation: Deriving from the parent: the national regime imposes genuine traveler-facing exposures — birth-sex passport/visa rules, officers instructed to refuse and consider lifetime fraud findings where 'reasonable doubt' on sex exists, restricted facilities in many states, and hostile federal custody policy — placing the parent near 0.45–0.55. This state adds documented, operating mitigations: no facility ban, a 2013 anti-discrimination act covering public accommodations and employment, a gender-identity hate-crime penalty enhancement, easy state marker change, and a current 'low-risk' classification (refrains from targeting). Those move it above the parent average into reduced risk. It cannot reach 0.85–0.95 because the national border/visa regime is a universal-exposure layer every visitor passes through (document disbelief, fraud findings, reported detentions of foreign trans citizens), and state custody placement is undocumented with national corrections guidance hostile. Open questions (X marker, panic-defence bill) are light. Result: 0.70 — protective local machinery inside a contested, partially hostile national regime.
